'''Ferdinando Mancini''' (born June 4, 1941) is an Italian [[theoretical physicist]], Emeritus Professor<ref>{{Cite web |title=FerdinandoMancini |url=https://www.fisica.unisa.it/Personal/HomepageE.asp?mancini}}</ref> in the Department of Physics at the [[University of Salerno]] and president<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=CVFerdinandoMancini |url=https://www.iiassvietri.it/en/storia-e-riconoscimenti/prof-ferdinando-mancini.html}}</ref> of the International Institute for Advanced Scientific Studies (IIASS)<ref name="iiassvietri.it">{{Cite web |title=International Institute for Advanced Scientific Studies (IIASS) |url=https://www.iiassvietri.it/en/}}</ref> in [[Vietri sul Mare]]. Mancini has contributed to [[condensed matter physics]], particularly the theory of strongly correlated systems<ref>{{Cite book |last=Mancini |first=Ferdinando |title=Out-Of-Equilibrium Physics of Correlated Electron Systems |date=2018 |publisher=Springer |others=Roberta Citro |isbn=978-3-319-94955-0 |editor-last=Mancini |editor-first=Ferdinando |series=Springer Series in Solid-State Sciences |location=}}</ref> and [[superconductivity]].

== Education and career ==
Mancini received his degree in Physics from the [[University of Naples Federico II]] in 1966.{{Citation needed|date=December 2025}} He then pursued doctoral studies in the United States, obtaining his Ph.D. in Physics from the [[University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee]] in 1971.{{Citation needed|date=December 2025}}

He joined the [[University of Salerno]] in 1972, where he was instrumental in the creation and development of its Faculty of Science. Mancini served as a Professor of Structure of Matter from 1980 until his retirement in 2011. In 2012, he was appointed Professor Emeritus by the University of Salerno.<ref name=":0" />

In addition to his roles at the university, Mancini helped founding the International Institute for Advanced Scientific Studies (IIASS)<ref name="iiassvietri.it"/> in Vietri sul Mare in 1981, alongside [[Eduardo R. Caianiello|Eduardo Caianiello]] and Maria Marinaro.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof.ssa Maria Marinaro |url=https://www.iiassvietri.it/it/storia-e-riconoscimenti/prof-ssa-maria-marianro.html}}</ref> The IIASS is an institute dedicated to advanced theoretical research.<ref>{{Cite web |title=La ricerca I.I.A.S.S |url=https://www.iiassvietri.it/it/ricerca.html |access-date= |website=www.iiassvietri.it}}</ref> Mancini has been president of the IIASS since 2012.

During his tenure at the [[University of Salerno]], Mancini also held administrative positions. He was the Director of the Department of Physics (later Department of Physics "E.R. Caianiello") for 12 years. For 10 years, he served as a member of the University's Board of Directors and as chairman of its Finance Committee.<ref name=":0" />

Mancini's scientific work and contribution to the field of [[condensed matter physics]] has been celebrated by his colleagues with a conference to mark his 60th birthday<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://archive.org/details/isbn_9780735401679 |title=Highlights in condensed matter physics: Proceedings of the International Conference HCMP03 held in Salerno at Arechi Castle from 9 to 11 May 2003 to celebrate the 60th birthday of Professor Ferdinando Mancini |date=2003 |publisher=Melville, N.Y. : American Institute of Physics |others=Internet Archive |isbn=978-0-7354-0167-9}}</ref>

== Research ==
Mancini's research interests include [[quantum field theory]], [[statistical mechanics]], and the physics of strongly correlated systems, with a focus on phenomena such as [[superconductivity]] and [[ferromagnetism]].<ref>{{Cite book |title=The Iron Pnictide Superconductors: An Introduction and Overview |date=2017 |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-3-319-56117-2 |editor-last=Mancini |editor-first=Ferdinando |series=Springer Series in Solid-State Sciences |location=Cham |editor-last2=Citro |editor-first2=Roberta}}</ref>

With [[Hiroomi Umezawa]], Mancini created and developed the boson method<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Leplae |first=L. |last2=Umezawa |first2=H. |last3=Mancini |first3=F. |date= |title=Derivation and application of the boson method in superconductivity |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0370157374900489 |journal=Physics Reports |language= |volume=10 |issue=4 |pages=151–272 |doi=10.1016/0370-1573(74)90048-9|url-access=subscription }}</ref> in superconductivity. This theoretical framework yielded results that demonstrated excellent agreement with experimental data. Later, his research focus shifted towards [[thermo field dynamics]], a quantum field theory at finite temperatures. He is credited with formulating the Composite Operator Method (COM),<ref>{{Citation |last=Avella |first=Adolfo |chapter=The Composite Operator Method (COM) |date=2012 |title=Strongly Correlated Systems |volume=171 |pages=103–141 |editor-last=Avella |editor-first=Adolfo |chapter-url=https://link.springer.com/10.1007/978-3-642-21831-6_4 |access-date=2025-05-18 |place=Berlin, Heidelberg |publisher=Springer Berlin Heidelberg |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-3-642-21831-6_4 |isbn=978-3-642-21830-9 |last2=Mancini |first2=Ferdinando |editor2-last=Mancini |editor2-first=Ferdinando|arxiv=1112.1103 }}</ref> a technique for analyzing strongly correlated systems like the [[Hubbard model]] and the [[Ising model]].

Mancini has co-edited about 30 academic volumes. Notable among these is the three-volume set 'Strongly Correlated Systems', covering theoretical methods,<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://www.worldcat.org/title/759585444 |title=Strongly correlated systems. Theoretical methods |date=2012 |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-3-642-21830-9 |editor-last=Avella |editor-first=Adolfo |series=Springer series in solid-state sciences |location=Heidelberg ; New York |oclc=759585444 |editor-last2=Mancini |editor-first2=Ferdinando}}</ref> numerical methods,<ref>{{Cite book |last=Avella |first=Adolfo |title=Strongly Correlated Systems: Numerical Methods |last2=Mancini |first2=Ferdinando |date=2013 |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-3-642-35105-1 |series=Springer Series in Solid-State Sciences |location=Berlin, Heidelberg}}</ref> and experimental techniques<ref>{{Cite book |last=Avella |first=Adolfo |title=Strongly Correlated Systems: Experimental Techniques |date=2015 |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-3-662-44132-9 |editor-last=Mancini |editor-first=Ferdinando |series=Springer Series in Solid-State Sciences |location=Berlin, Heidelberg}}</ref> for studying these complex systems.
